purpose: The band under the Contact title band: the team lanes side by side (Sales and Support), each with its scope in one sentence and the action that reaches that team, over a row of self-serve channels. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'contact-hub-section', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `module`, `registration-frame`, `card-grid`, `feature-item`, `button` and `status-indicator`. Lanes and channels share one frame, the channels in the rows under the lanes. A lane can carry a second button and a link to the system status page, so a reader can check for an incident before opening a ticket.
useWhen: On the Contact page, to route a reader to the team or channel that answers them.
avoidWhen: For a closing ask at the end of a page → use `closing-call-to-action-section`.
For a grid of product use cases → use `customer-use-cases-section`.
related: `feature-item` — each self-serve channel is a linked topic.
`customer-use-cases-section` — the sibling band of icon-led topics.
bestPractices: Give it as many lanes and channels as the page has: both rows balance themselves (`card-grid` `layout: 'balanced'`), so two channels split the row in halves, three in thirds, four into 2 × 2 and five into 3 + 2, with no empty cell.
Don't pad `channels` to three or drop one to make the row fit.
Put an emergency channel (an attack in progress) first and give it `severity: 'danger'`, so a reader under attack finds it at a glance; no other channel takes a severity.
Keep each lane's description to one sentence that states what that team handles.
Set `target: '_blank'` on a channel or status link that leaves the site.
Lead each lane with its `action`; add a `secondaryAction` only for a second route to the same team (an outlined button after the first).
Give the band an `anchor` when a page links to it with a `#hash`.
